title: 2019 AMC 10A Problem 21
statement: A sphere with center \(O\) has radius \(6.\) A triangle with sides of length \(15,\) \(15,\) and \(24\) is situated in space so that each of its sides is tangent to the sphere. What is the distance between \(O\) and the plane determined by the triangle?

solutions.text:
The altitude to the side of length \(24\) is \[\sqrt{15^2-12^2}=9,\] so the triangle has area \(\frac12\cdot24\cdot9=108\) and semiperimeter \(27\). Its inradius is therefore \[r=\frac{108}{27}=4.\]

Let \(P\) be the perpendicular projection of \(O\) onto the triangle’s plane, and let \(d=OP\). Because all three side-lines are tangent to the sphere, \(P\) is the incenter and its perpendicular distance to each side is \(4\). The distance from \(O\) to each side-line is the sphere’s radius, \(6\), so the Pythagorean theorem gives \[d^2+4^2=6^2.\] Hence \(d=2\sqrt5.\)

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: Take a cross-section perpendicular to the triangle plane
The inradius of the triangle controls the tangent distance to the sphere
